oneliner.t: Green Party nominee who won the July 21, 2026 Green primary as a write-in with 5 votes; the Arizona Green Party says it actively opposes his candidacy. He was arrested Sept 19, 2026 and charged with threatening a Superior Court judge and an attorney's office and with computer tampering; he has not been convicted.

upbringing.t: Per his own Ballotpedia profile: born in Bloomington, Indiana, attended Sunnyslope High School in Phoenix, and later earned degrees from Glendale Community College, Arizona State University and Northern Arizona University. He describes himself as a public-school teacher, small-business owner and disability advocate who turned to conservatorship-reform advocacy after a debilitating injury. These details are self-reported and were not independently confirmed.

legal.t: Contacted by the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office Threat Management Unit and booked into jail on Sept 19, 2026. Per KTAR, charged with two felonies (using an electronic communication to intimidate, threaten or harass; computer tampering) and one misdemeanor (threatening or intimidating); AZFamily, citing court records, describes multiple counts of threatening or intimidating plus one count of computer tampering. Prosecutors say he sent threatening emails mentioning guns to a Superior Court judge and an attorney's office; they said no gun was recovered. The sheriff's office says he admitted sending the communications. Bond was set at $150,000 and the arrest documents were sealed to protect the victims. Felony class and case number were not reported.
legal.short: Charged: threats to judge, computer tampering
legal.status: Charged, not convicted. A hearing was set for about Sept 24, 2026; no plea, indictment, release or later status was reported as of 2026-10-08.

research_notes: PARTY STATUS: The Arizona Green Party rates his candidacy 'actively opposed'; a spokesperson cited a 'consistent pattern of abusive behavior' and said he had been banned from the Arizona Democratic Party and Democratic Socialists of Phoenix. That is the party's statement and was not independently verified. He is NOT among the Green candidates (Lombardo, Collier) that KJZZ's July 30 report linked to Republican operatives. COUNT DISCREPANCY: AZFamily's photo caption says two counts of threatening or intimidating; its text says 'multiple'; KTAR lists one felony electronic-threat count, one felony computer-tampering count and one misdemeanor threatening count. Recorded as charges only. Ballotpedia's profile (AZ-01, Democratic, Aug 4 primary) predates his move to the CD3 Green line.
